fact.flowerLifespanDesc: Male flowers last only one day while female flowers can remain receptive for 2-3 days.
fact.wateringNeedsDesc: Gourds need consistent moisture, especially during flowering and fruiting stages.
fact.sunlightDesc: Gourds require at least 6-8 hours of direct sunlight daily.
fact.pollinationSuccessDesc: Hand pollination in the early morning has the highest success rate.
fact.daysToMaturityDesc: Most gourd varieties reach maturity in 60-90 days from planting.
fact.temperatureDesc: Gourds grow best in temperatures between 25-35°C.

guide.malePoint1: Male flowers have a thin, straight stem.
guide.malePoint2: They appear earlier in the plant's life cycle.
guide.malePoint3: Male flowers are more numerous than female flowers.
guide.malePoint5: Male flowers typically open in the morning.
guide.femalePoint1: Female flowers have a small swollen base (the ovary).
guide.femalePoint2: They are typically fewer in number than male flowers.
guide.femalePoint3: Female flowers open for only one day.
guide.femalePoint4: They require pollination within a few hours of opening.
guide.femalePoint5: Each female flower can produce one fruit.
guide.visualPoint1: Male flowers have long, thin stems.
guide.visualPoint2: Female flowers have a round swelling at the base.
guide.visualPoint3: Female flowers tend to be larger in size.
guide.bestTimePoint1: Early morning (6-9 AM) is ideal when flowers are fully open.
guide.bestTimePoint2: High humidity during morning keeps pollen viable longer.
guide.bestTimePoint3: Avoid mid-day heat as pollen becomes less viable.
guide.stepPoint1: Identify male and female flowers in the morning.
guide.stepPoint2: Gently pick a male flower and remove the petals.
guide.stepPoint3: Transfer pollen directly to the female flower.
guide.stepPoint4: Alternatively, use a small brush to transfer pollen.
guide.stepPoint5: Mark the pollinated female flower for tracking.
guide.successTip1: Use multiple male flowers to ensure good pollination.
guide.successTip2: Pollinate within the first 2 hours of flower opening.
guide.successTip4: Provide adequate nutrition and water to support fruit development.
guide.visualSignPoint1: The fruit changes from dark green to its mature color.
guide.visualSignPoint2: The skin becomes harder and less glossy.
guide.visualSignPoint3: The stem starts to dry and turn brown.
guide.visualSignPoint4: The fruit reaches its expected size.
guide.physicalTestPoint1: Gently squeeze the fruit - it should feel firm.
guide.physicalTestPoint2: Check for uniform color development across the surface.
guide.physicalTestPoint3: Taste a small sample if you're growing edible varieties.
guide.physicalTestPoint4: Weigh the fruit to ensure it meets expected size.
guide.harvestTimingPoint1: Most gourds are ready to harvest 45-60 days after pollination.
guide.harvestTimingPoint2: Look for color changes and hardening of the skin.
guide.harvestTimingPoint3: Use a sharp knife or pruning shears to cut the stem.
guide.harvestTimingPoint4: Harvest in the morning when temperatures are cooler.
guide.poorFruitPoint1: Poor pollination due to lack of pollinators.
guide.fruitRotPoint1: Caused by fungal infections in wet conditions.
guide.fruitRotPoint2: Ensure proper spacing between plants for air circulation.
guide.fruitRotPoint3: Avoid overhead watering to keep fruits dry.
guide.fruitRotPoint4: Remove affected fruits immediately to prevent spread.
guide.yellowingPoint1: May indicate nitrogen deficiency in the soil.
guide.yellowingPoint2: Check for overwatering or poor drainage.

howToUse.title: Learn How to Use
howToUse.masterDesc: Follow this 5-step process for the best scanning results
howToUse.step1Desc: Clean the flower or leaf with a soft, dry cloth. Remove any dirt or water droplets.
howToUse.step2Desc: Natural sunlight works best. Avoid harsh shadows directly on the plant part.
howToUse.step3Desc: Hold 15-20cm away. Ensure the flower or leaf fills most of the frame.
howToUse.step4Desc: Tap capture and keep the camera steady. Our AI will analyze your scan in seconds.
howToUse.step5Desc: Check the variety, confidence score, and health insights. Save to track progress!
howToUse.askTakoDesc: Your AI learning assistant is ready to help
howToUse.takoGreeting: Hi! I'm Tako 🪴 Your learning guide for gourd scanning and farming. Ask me anything!
howToUse.faqDesc: Find answers to common questions about scanning, tracking, and gourd cultivation.
howToUse.faq1A: Navigate to the Camera tab, point your camera at a gourd flower or leaf, and tap the capture button.
howToUse.faq2Q: What types of gourds can I scan?
howToUse.faq2A: You can scan Bitter Gourd, Bottle Gourd, Sponge Gourd, Cucumber, and Squash.
howToUse.faq3Q: How do I get the best scan results?
howToUse.faq3A: Use good lighting, hold the camera steady 15-20cm away, and ensure the gourd fills most of the frame.
howToUse.faq4Q: What should I do if the camera is not focusing?
howToUse.faq4A: Clean your camera lens, ensure adequate lighting, and tap on the screen to focus.
howToUse.faq5Q: Can I view my scan history?
howToUse.faq5A: Yes, go to the Profile tab and tap on History to view all your past scans.
howToUse.faq6Q: How do I compare previous scans?
howToUse.faq6A: In the History tab, select two scans to view them side by side and track progress.
howToUse.faq7A: Go to the Pollination tab, select your plant, and tap Add Pollination to record the event.
howToUse.faq8Q: What does the confidence score mean?
howToUse.faq8A: The confidence score indicates how certain the AI is about its prediction. Higher scores mean more reliable results.
howToUse.faq9Q: What should I do if the analysis fails?
howToUse.faq9A: Try scanning again with better lighting and a steadier camera. If the issue persists, check your internet connection.
howToUse.faq10Q: Why is the app not loading?
howToUse.faq10A: Check your internet connection, restart the app, or contact support if the problem continues.
howToUse.learningCheckpointsDesc: Complete each checkpoint to master gourd scanning and cultivation.
